angularDiameterSource: Computed here from the record's radius and distance: 2 x 890,496 km at 141.86 pc = 0.08 mas. No interferometric diameter of this star is used.
distanceSource: Gaia DR3 parallax 7.0495 +/- 0.0114 mas (same row, RUWE 0.88): 141.86 pc, no zero-point correction
radiusSource: Radius 1.28 +/- 0.03 solar radii from Jordán et al. 2020, the stellar radius of the default parameter set of TOI-677 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..145J/abstract): 890,496 km at 695,700 km per solar radius. Mass 1.181 +/- 0.058 solar masses from Jordán et al. 2020, the stellar mass of the default parameter set of TOI-677 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..145J/abstract); GM is that mass times the JPL solar GM. Temperature 6295 +/- 77 K from Jordán et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-677 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..145J/abstract). presentationUp: the display axis is a sky-plane convention; the spin axis's position angle on the sky is not measured.
effectiveTemperatureSource: Jordán et al. 2020, the stellar temperature of the default parameter set of TOI-677 b in the NASA Exoplanet Archive (https://ui.adsabs.harvard.edu/abs/2020AJ....159..145J/abstract)
surfaceGravitySource: log g from the mass and radius in packages/astronomy/data/bodies/toi-677.json (sources in its physicalNotes), log10(GM/R^2) in cgs: 4.296, rounded to two decimals

shape.qualification: A sphere at the published radius, coloured from the star's Gaia DR3 BP/RP spectrum (photometry/stellar-color.json); no image of the photosphere exists.
